meta.purpose: DataCenter re-tag, 19 October 2026, under ruling 6 of 18 October: a tie through a power plant counts when the plant's filings, developer, or utility tie that plant to data center load. Covers the US gas rows in development whose DataCenter was blank, the 16 big interstate expansions first (plan docs/plans/2026-10-16_us-gas-datacenter-subfloor.md).

values.DataCenterNotes: The pipeline expansion supplies the Tennessee Valley Authority's new gas plant at the Kingston site in Tennessee. In February 2026 the authority said growing demand from data centers, population, and employment drove its decision to build the plant and keep the Kingston coal units running longer. The two sources are Enbridge's project page for the pipeline and a February 2026 news report on the authority's board vote.

verifications.note: Enbridge page says the project supplies gas for the Kingston plant replacement.
Television station report on the February 2026 board vote. The authority says demand growth driven by data centers, population, and employment created the need for the new gas plant at Kingston.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The pipeline serves the new Tennessee Valley Authority gas plant at Kingston. The authority named data center growth among the reasons for that plant. No single data center campus is named, so this is an indirect tie. The earlier pass found nothing because it looked only at the pipeline pages.

values.DataCenterNotes: A January 2026 trade report on the Intensity and Rainbow Energy Center announcement says the pipeline project, which includes the 208-mile Phase II extension from Washburn to Casselton, is meant to support sustained data center growth, grid reliability needs, and industrial development in North Dakota. The data center wording covers the project as a whole and no data center customer is named for Phase II.

verifications.note: Names the Intensity and Rainbow pipeline and its Phase II extension, and says the approach supports sustained data center growth.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The developers say the whole pipeline project supports data center growth, and the same article describes Phase II. The wording is general and mostly tied to Phase I and the Coal Creek power hub, so this is a judgment call. Earlier passes left it blank.

values.DataCenterNotes: Pipeline and Gas Journal reported in July 2025 that Northwest Pipeline's FERC application for the Wild Trail Project says the project was developed in response to strong demand to serve coal-to-gas power conversions, data centers, and industrial loads. No specific data center or plant is named.

verifications.note: Article on the Wild Trail Project says the application cites demand from coal-to-gas power conversions, data centers, and industrial loads.

resolutions.researcher_notes: A trade press article on the company's federal filing lists data centers among the reasons for the project. The company's own page and the federal notice do not say it. No named data center was found.

values.DataCenterNotes: The lateral delivers gas to the new Broadwing Energy plant in Decatur, Illinois, and to an Archer Daniels Midland facility, per a May 2025 federal notice. A Power Engineering report says Google will buy most of the Broadwing plant's power for its data centers, and ESG Today says the deal is meant to cover the energy needs of Google's growing data center footprint. No specific campus is named.

verifications.note: Federal notice for the Decatur Lateral says it delivers gas to Archer Daniels Midland and the Broadwing power facility.
Says Google will buy the majority of the Decatur, Illinois gas plant's power for its data centers.
Says the Broadwing deal addresses the energy needs of Google's data center footprint; plant on ADM site in Decatur.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The Decatur lateral feeds the Broadwing plant. Google has agreed to buy most of that plant's power and says it is for its data centers. Two trade press sources say so. No single data center campus is named, and the pipeline filing itself does not mention data centers.

values.DataCenterNotes: When Kinder Morgan launched the binding open season for this project in July 2024, its chief executive said the open season was part of meeting new gas demand for electric generation tied to artificial intelligence, cryptocurrency mining, data centers, and industrial reshoring. Data centers are one of several named drivers. No utility shipper or power plant fed by this expansion was found with its own data center tie.

verifications.note: A trade press article on the open season for South System Expansion 4. It quotes Kinder Morgan chief executive Kimberly Dang saying the open season is part of meeting new gas demand for power generation associated with artificial intelligence, crypto mining, data centers, and industrial reshoring.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The tag rests on the developer's own statement at the start of the project, which names data centers among several demand drivers. It is about this project's open season, not company-wide talk. The named shippers are the Tennessee Valley Authority, Oglethorpe Power, Dominion Energy South Carolina, Southern Company Services, Atlanta Gas Light, and Santee Cooper. The Southern Company and Oglethorpe plants are not named. Dominion Energy South Carolina says 290,000 dekatherms a day of its share is meant for the Canadys Station gas plant, which it co-owns with Santee Cooper. Only critics, such as the Southern Environmental Law Center, and a speculative data center developer link Canadys to data center load. The utilities' own approval releases do not mention data centers, and the data center developer said in September 2026 that it is not tied to Canadys. So the plant link is not used. The August 2026 Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approval article mentions data centers only in the opponents' arguments.

values.DataCenterNotes: The pipeline would carry gas to the planned 2,200 megawatt Dominion Energy and Santee Cooper gas plant on the former Canadys coal site in Colleton County, South Carolina. A May 2026 SC Daily Gazette report says utility executives call the plant essential for rapid population and industrial growth, and the reporter adds that this growth includes a ballooning number of energy-intensive data centers. The utilities' own approval statements found do not mention data centers. No single data center is named as a customer.

verifications.note: October 2025 news report says Santee Cooper and Dominion contracted Kinder Morgan to build the $431 million pipeline from Screven County, Georgia, to the Canadys plant site.

May 2026 news report says the plant is needed amid growth that includes a ballooning number of energy-intensive data centers, and that the Kinder Morgan pipeline will feed it. Read through a Wayback copy because the live site blocks plain fetches.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The Kinder Morgan Bridge pipeline feeds the Canadys gas plant. Utility executives name data centers among the reasons for the plant. Both refs are from the same newspaper, so they are not independent. No named data center customer was found. Judgment call: the data center line in the Gazette is the reporter's summary, not a direct utility quote. A separate pass on South System Expansion 4 found that a data center developer said in September 2026 it is not tied to Canadys, and that otherwise only critics link Canadys to data centers.

values.DataCenterNotes: The expansion includes a 14.64 mile branch line and a new meter station for the Nebraska Public Power District Princeton Road power station, per a Federal Register notice from May 2026. The district's own page on its new generation says it expects unprecedented load growth and that much of the business interest it sees comes from agriculture-related operations and data centers. No single data center customer is named.

verifications.note: Federal Register notice of the Central Mainline Corridor Expansion lists the Nebraska Public Power District Princeton Road power station branch line and meter station.
District page on new generation at Princeton Road Station cites load growth and says business interest comes from ag-related operations and data centers.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The pipeline branch line serves the Princeton Road power station. The district says data centers are among the sources of the load growth behind its new generation. It does not name a specific data center, so this is a medium-strength tie.

values.DataCenterNotes: The pipeline connects the Mountain Valley Southgate project to Duke Energy Progress's new gas plant in Person County near Roxboro, and serves only that plant. A Canary Media report from February 2025 says the Person County plant is designed in part to meet rising demand expected from data centers and large new customers. No named data center customer was found.

verifications.note: North Carolina Newsline brief from February 2024 names the T15 Reliability Project and says it connects MVP Southgate with Duke Energy's planned new gas power plants near Roxboro.
Southern Alliance for Clean Energy primer says the T15 pipeline will supply Duke's proposed Roxboro gas plant and serves only one plant.
Canary Media says the new Person County gas plant is designed in part to meet rising demand expected from data centers and large new customers. The article does not use the word Roxboro in its text.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The tie runs through the power plant. The pipeline serves Duke's new gas plant in Person County near Roxboro. Canary Media says that plant is meant in part for data center demand. The Canary Media article does not say Roxboro in its text, so the match rests on Person County and the second phase of the plant approved the year before. No named customer was found.

values.DataCenterNotes: The Wisconsin commission case page for the Paris engine plant places the seven gas engines, up to 128 megawatts, at the Lakeshore Capacity Improvement Project regulator station in the Town of Paris, which is the end of the Lakeshore Lateral. A Milwaukee public radio report on the May 2025 commission approval of the Paris and Oak Creek plants says We Energies points to a Microsoft data center being built in Racine County, and one commissioner cited data centers in southeastern Wisconsin as a reason for his vote.

verifications.note: Case page for the Paris engine plant. Puts the plant at the Lakeshore Capacity Improvement Project regulator station in the Town of Paris. Does not mention data centers.
Says We Energies points to a Microsoft data center in Racine County as a reason for the plants, and a commissioner cited data centers. Does not name the Lakeshore pipeline.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The Lakeshore Lateral was approved in 2020 and built in 2021 for regional demand, so it was not planned for the data center. It now ends at the site of the new Paris engine plant, which We Energies and the commission tied to the Microsoft data center in Mount Pleasant. The link between the pipeline and the plant rests on the plant being sited at the Lakeshore regulator station. No page says in one sentence that the lateral feeds the plant, so please review. The pipeline source and the data center source are different pages.

values.DataCenterNotes: The pipeline is the 19-mile service line that carries gas from the MountainWest Pipeline to the Aquila power plant in Eagle Mountain, Utah, being built by Williams. A February 2026 Eagle Mountain city hearing notice says Williams plans a natural gas power plant on the Stadion parcel to serve the Meta data center expansion. The notice does not use the name Aquila. The match rests on Williams, the Eagle Mountain location, and the Aquila project description in the Williams shipper meeting slides.

verifications.note: Williams shipper advisory slides from April 2026 describe Project Aquila in Eagle Mountain, Utah, with a 19-mile service pipeline from MountainWest to the power plant and a 1-mile line from Kern River.
Eagle Mountain notice of public hearings for February 24, 2026 says Williams will co-locate a natural gas power facility on the Stadion parcel to facilitate the Meta data center expansion.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The pipeline serves the Aquila power plant in Eagle Mountain, Utah. A city hearing notice ties a Williams gas plant there to the Meta data center expansion. The notice never says Aquila, so the link is by company and place. A Utah utility commission filing from November 2025 also describes Aquila and says it will be co-located with a customer's industrial property, but it does not name the customer.

values.DataCenterNotes: The Wisconsin commission case page for the Rochester Lateral says the pipeline will give firm gas to the proposed Oak Creek combustion turbine plant and the Paris engine plant, and later to the Elm Road station. A Milwaukee public radio report on the May 2025 commission approval of the Oak Creek and Paris plants says We Energies cited growing demand, including an incoming Microsoft data center in Racine County. A University of Wisconsin extension article gives the same link.

verifications.note: Case page for the Rochester Lateral. States the need is firm gas for the Oak Creek Combustion Turbine, the Paris engine plant, and later the Elm Road station.
Says the commission approved the Oak Creek and Paris plants and We Energies points to a Microsoft data center being built in Racine County as a reason.
Page loaded and mentions data centers in connection with the approved plants.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The Rochester Lateral supplies the new Oak Creek gas turbine plant and the Paris engine plant. We Energies and the state commission tied those plants to the Microsoft data center in Mount Pleasant. The commission page and the radio report are different publishers.
